title: Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development
key_facts: GitHub says it is rebuilding the Git infrastructure behind its repositories because developers and AI agents now work in them at the same time.
Total Git activity grew from 218.2 billion events a month to 473.3 billion between September 2025 and August 2026.
In September 2026 developers and agents made 7.38 billion commits, more than five times a year earlier.
The current system (Spokes) keeps five full copies of each repository, so adding copies for reads makes writes slower.
GitHub says the new design separates storage durability from read capacity.
In internal benchmarks it reports up to 35 times higher write throughput; a follow-up post is promised.
quote_evidence: In September alone, developers and agents made 7.38 billion commits on GitHub, more than five times as many as a year earlier.
In internal benchmarks, it has delivered up to 35 times higher write throughput, with read capacity that scales on its own to meet demand.
why_it_matters_hint: The busiest repositories are hitting limits of the old design as AI agents multiply the number of changes.
notes: Company engineering blog; the 35x figure is an internal benchmark and the new system is not yet released. Score lowered 7 to 6: describes work in progress, not a launch.
